nodes.action: Create an ensemble of EfficientNet-B0 and ResNet-18 models, each with a spatial attention module. Use 5-fold stratified cross-validation, RandAugment and CutMix augmentations, BCEWithLogitsLoss, AdamW optimizer with warmup and cosine annealing scheduler. Average predictions from all folds and both models for final submission.
applies_when: When wanting to improve robustness and generalization beyond a single model for aerial cactus identification.

nodes.title: Set DataLoader num_workers=0 to avoid shared memory issues in containerized environments
nodes.action: Set num_workers=0 and pin_memory=False in DataLoader to avoid shared memory (shm) exhaustion, which causes bus errors and worker crashes. This trades off data loading speed for reliability.
applies_when: When running in environments with limited shared memory (e.g., Docker containers, Kaggle notebooks) and experiencing DataLoader worker crashes due to shm issues.

nodes.action: Check PyTorch version before using label_smoothing with BCEWithLogitsLoss. If version < 1.10, implement label smoothing manually or use standard BCEWithLogitsLoss without label_smoothing.
applies_when: When using BCEWithLogitsLoss with label smoothing in environments where PyTorch version may be older than 1.10 (label_smoothing parameter introduced in PyTorch 1.10).

nodes.action: When accessing the hidden size of a SigLIP model from HuggingFace, use 'hidden_size' (with the typo) instead of 'hidden_size' as the config attribute. Alternatively, access via 'vision_config.hidden_size'.
applies_when: When working with SigLIP models (e.g., google/siglip2-so400m-patch16-256) from HuggingFace transformers and needing to get the hidden dimension for classifier head construction.

nodes.title: Ensure SigLIP model receives both pixel_values and input_ids for forward pass
nodes.action: When using a multimodal SigLIP model (vision-language), provide both pixel_values and input_ids to the forward method. For vision-only tasks, use a vision-only backbone (e.g., from timm) or extract image features using the vision encoder separately.
applies_when: When using SigLIP2 or similar vision-language models for image-only classification tasks, as they expect both image and text inputs.

nodes.title: Avoid using RandAugment with magnitude parameter in older timm versions
nodes.action: Use torchvision.transforms.TrivialAugmentWide instead of timm.data.RandAugment when the installed timm version does not support the magnitude parameter. Alternatively, omit the magnitude parameter and use default settings.
applies_when: When using RandAugment from timm and encountering TypeError about unexpected keyword argument 'magnitude', indicating an older timm version.

nodes.title: Avoid computing train AUC when mixup augmentation produces continuous labels
nodes.action: Skip computing training AUC when mixup augmentation is applied, as the continuous labels (floats between 0 and 1) are incompatible with roc_auc_score which expects binary labels. Only compute validation AUC on non-mixed batches.
applies_when: When using mixup augmentation during training and attempting to compute training AUC with sklearn's roc_auc_score.

nodes.action: When adding pseudo-labeled test samples to the training set, ensure the dataset loader can access images from both train and test directories. Either copy test images to the train directory or modify the dataset to accept a list of image paths with corresponding directories.
applies_when: When implementing pseudo-labeling that adds test samples to the training set for retraining, to avoid FileNotFoundError due to incorrect image directory.

nodes.title: Use correct indexing for EfficientNet backbone blocks when unfreezing
nodes.action: When unfreezing specific blocks of an EfficientNet backbone from timm, iterate over the blocks list and unfreeze the last N blocks by index (e.g., for EfficientNet-B0, blocks are indexed 0-6, so unfreeze blocks[4:] for last 3 blocks). Use len(backbone.blocks) to determine the total number of blocks.
applies_when: When implementing partial fine-tuning of EfficientNet models from timm and needing to unfreeze specific blocks by index.

nodes.title: Use correct classifier head dimensions for EfficientNet-V2-S backbone
nodes.action: When replacing the classifier head of EfficientNet-V2-S from timm, use the backbone's in_features attribute (e.g., 1280) for the first linear layer. Avoid adding extra pooling layers as the backbone already includes adaptive average pooling.
applies_when: When customizing the classifier head of EfficientNet-V2-S from timm and encountering shape mismatches due to incorrect in_features.

nodes.title: Ensure labels are float type for BCEWithLogitsLoss
nodes.action: Convert target labels to float type (e.g., batch_y.float()) before passing to BCEWithLogitsLoss, as it expects float targets. Avoid using Long type which can cause type mismatch errors.
applies_when: When using BCEWithLogitsLoss and encountering 'result type Float can't be cast to the desired output type Long' error.

nodes.action: Use gradient clipping (max_norm=1.0) and add input validation (e.g., clamp inputs to valid range) to prevent NaN values in model outputs. Also ensure mixed precision training uses consistent autocast context and proper GradScaler usage.
applies_when: When model produces NaN predictions during training or validation, often due to numerical instability or exploding gradients.

nodes.action: When using DINOv2 ViT-Large model from timm (vit_large_patch14_dinov2.lvd142m), resize input images to 518x518 as required by the model. Using smaller sizes (e.g., 224x224) will cause assertion errors.

nodes.action: Extract overlapping patches (e.g., 64x64 with stride 32) from full-resolution images, train on patches, and reconstruct full images by weighted averaging of overlapping predictions to preserve high-frequency details and avoid resolution loss.
applies_when: When working with image denoising tasks where full-image resizing destroys fine details and training data is limited.

nodes.action: Implement a U-Net autoencoder with Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) blocks in encoder/decoder, Gaussian noise injection, dropout, and skip connections. Train with a combined loss of MSE (or L1) and SSIM to improve perceptual quality and reduce RMSE.

nodes.title: Use noise prior input channel (median filter residual) to improve denoising
nodes.action: Compute a noise prior map as the residual between the noisy image and its median-filtered version, and stack it as an additional input channel (e.g., 2-channel input) to provide explicit noise information to the model.
applies_when: When denoising images with structured noise and the model benefits from explicit noise estimation.

nodes.action: Train initially on larger patches (e.g., 128x128) to learn global context, then switch to smaller patches (e.g., 64x64) to refine fine details, using a curriculum learning schedule.
applies_when: When training a denoising model and the model struggles to capture both global structure and fine details simultaneously.

nodes.action: Add attention gates (e.g., additive attention) to the skip connections of a U-Net to suppress irrelevant features and enhance important spatial regions, improving denoising quality.

nodes.action: Ensure all images in a batch have the same spatial dimensions by applying deterministic resizing or cropping after random augmentations, or by using a custom collate function that handles variable sizes.
applies_when: When using DataLoader with random augmentations that may change image dimensions (e.g., RandomAffine, RandomRotation).

nodes.title: Use DINOv2 ViT-L/14 with gated multimodal fusion for leaf classification
nodes.action: Use DINOv2 ViT-L/14 as frozen image feature extractor (1024-dim), engineer extensive tabular features (raw values, per-group statistics, cross-group interactions, PCA), and train a multimodal classifier with separate projectors for tabular and image modalities, a learnable gating fusion mechanism, and a classifier head with label smoothing cross-entropy loss. nodes.title: Use ensemble of XGBoost, MLP on image features, and Logistic Regression with optimized weights
nodes.action: Train three models: XGBoost on engineered tabular features, an MLP on SigLIP2 image embeddings, and a Logistic Regression with polynomial features. Optimize ensemble weights via grid search on validation log loss to minimize the metric.

nodes.action: When using Vision Transformers (e.g., DINOv2 with patch size 14), resize images to dimensions that are multiples of the patch size (e.g., 224, 252) to avoid assertion errors in patch embedding.

nodes.action: Place all function definitions at the top of the script, before any code that calls them, to avoid NameError due to Python's top-to-bottom execution order.

nodes.action: Ensure each function is defined only once in the script. Duplicate definitions can cause confusion and bugs due to the later definition overriding the earlier one.

nodes.title: Avoid data leakage by fitting PCA and scalers on training fold only
nodes.action: When performing dimensionality reduction (PCA) or scaling, fit the transformation on the training fold only, then transform validation and test sets using the fitted object. Do not fit separately on each split.
applies_when: When applying PCA or StandardScaler in cross-validation or train/validation splits.

nodes.title: Avoid CatBoost random_seed and random_state conflict
nodes.action: When using CatBoostClassifier, do not set both 'random_seed' and 'random_state' parameters simultaneously. Use only 'random_state' for consistency.
applies_when: When configuring CatBoost models in scikit-learn pipelines.

nodes.title: Use per-group PCA and separate scaling for structured tabular features
nodes.action: Split features into groups (e.g., margin, shape, texture), apply StandardScaler and PCA (retaining 95% variance) independently per group to preserve group-specific structure and reduce dimensionality without mixing information.
applies_when: When dealing with tabular data that has natural feature groupings (e.g., leaf margin/shape/texture) and a small sample size relative to feature dimension.

nodes.title: Use multi-branch MLP with per-group branches and cross-attention fusion
nodes.action: Design a neural network with separate MLP branches for each feature group (e.g., margin, shape, texture), then fuse via cross-attention mechanism followed by a classifier head. Use moderate dropout (0.3) and batch normalization.
applies_when: When tabular features have natural groupings and a multi-branch architecture can capture inter-group interactions.

nodes.title: Use test-time augmentation (TTA) with small noise for inference
nodes.action: During inference, generate multiple perturbed versions of each test sample (e.g., add Gaussian noise to features) and average the predictions to improve robustness and reduce variance.

nodes.title: Use CosineAnnealingLR scheduler with warmup for stable training
nodes.action: Implement a cosine annealing learning rate schedule with a linear warmup phase (e.g., 5 epochs) to gradually increase LR then decay, helping convergence.

nodes.title: Use early stopping based on validation log loss to prevent overfitting
nodes.action: Monitor validation log loss each epoch and stop training if it does not improve for a patience number of epochs (e.g., 30), restoring the best model weights.
applies_when: When training neural networks on small datasets to avoid overfitting and save time.

nodes.title: Use AdamW optimizer with weight decay for regularization
nodes.action: Use torch.optim.AdamW with weight_decay=1e-4 to apply decoupled weight decay, improving generalization.

nodes.title: Use gradient clipping to stabilize training and avoid NaN losses
nodes.action: Apply torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=1.0) after loss.backward() to prevent gradient explosion.
applies_when: When training deep networks, especially with mixup or complex architectures, to avoid numerical instability.

nodes.title: Avoid data leakage by fitting scalers and PCA on training fold only
nodes.action: Within each cross-validation fold, fit StandardScaler and PCA exclusively on the training subset, then transform both train and validation subsets. Never use the full dataset before splitting.

nodes.title: Avoid using statistical features computed per-sample across the whole dataset before splitting
nodes.action: Do not compute per-sample statistics (e.g., mean, std, skewness) on the full dataset before train/validation split, as they leak information from other samples. Compute them within each fold's training data only.
applies_when: When engineering features that involve per-sample aggregations across the dataset.

nodes.title: Ensure loss tensor is scalar before calling backward()

When the target variable has a long tail and log transformation helps normalize the distribution.

nodes.title: Use XGBoost with standard squared error objective for fare prediction
nodes.action: Use 'reg:squarederror' objective for XGBoost instead of 'reg:pseudohubererror' to avoid divergence, and clip predictions before applying expm1 to prevent overflow.
applies_when: When training XGBoost for regression on log-transformed fare with large dataset.

When training XGBoost for regression on log-transformed fare with large dataset.

nodes.title: Process validation data in batches to avoid CUDA OOM
nodes.action: When validating a neural network on a large dataset, process validation data in batches (same as training) instead of a single forward pass to avoid out-of-memory errors.
applies_when: When using GPU for neural network inference on a large validation set.
nodes.text:
Process validation data in batches to avoid CUDA OOM

nodes.title: Avoid passing verbose_eval as keyword argument to lgb.train
nodes.action: Use the 'verbose' parameter in the model params dict or lgb.log_evaluation callback instead of passing verbose_eval as a keyword argument to lgb.train.
applies_when: When using LightGBM's train function and wanting to control logging verbosity.
nodes.text:
Avoid passing verbose_eval as keyword argument to lgb.train
Use the 'verbose' parameter in the model params dict or lgb.log_evaluation callback instead of passing verbose_eval as a keyword argument to lgb.train.
When using LightGBM's train function and wanting to control logging verbosity.

nodes.title: Use smaller model variant to avoid CUDA OOM
nodes.action: When encountering CUDA out-of-memory errors, switch to a smaller model variant (e.g., DeBERTa-v3-small or ModernBERT-base instead of DeBERTa-v3-large or ModernBERT-large) and reduce batch size (e.g., batch_size=8), max sequence length (e.g., max_length=256), and gradient accumulation steps to fit GPU memory.
applies_when: When GPU memory is insufficient for a large transformer model, causing CUDA OOM errors during training.
nodes.text:
Use smaller model variant to avoid CUDA OOM
When encountering CUDA out-of-memory errors, switch to a smaller model variant (e.g., DeBERTa-v3-small or ModernBERT-base instead of DeBERTa-v3-large or ModernBERT-large) and reduce batch size (e.g., batch_size=8), max sequence length (e.g., max_length=256), and gradient accumulation steps to fit GPU memory.
When GPU memory is insufficient for a large transformer model, causing CUDA OOM errors during training.

nodes.title: Freeze backbone and use XGBoost on embeddings to avoid overfitting
nodes.action: Extract frozen transformer embeddings (e.g., [CLS] token) and train an XGBoost classifier with multi:softprob objective, early stopping, and cross-validation. This avoids fine-tuning instability and overfitting.
applies_when: When fine-tuning a large transformer leads to severe overfitting or training instability.
nodes.text:
Freeze backbone and use XGBoost on embeddings to avoid overfitting
Extract frozen transformer embeddings (e.g., [CLS] token) and train an XGBoost classifier with multi:softprob objective, early stopping, and cross-validation. This avoids fine-tuning instability and overfitting.
When fine-tuning a large transformer leads to severe overfitting or training instability.

nodes.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-base with partial freezing and label smoothing
nodes.action: Fine-tune DeBERTa-v3-base with the first 8 layers frozen, label smoothing (0.1), gradient clipping, mixed precision, and early stopping. Use a single 90/10 stratified split for more epochs.
applies_when: When fine-tuning a medium-sized transformer for text classification with limited data.
nodes.text:
Use DeBERTa-v3-base with partial freezing and label smoothing
Fine-tune DeBERTa-v3-base with the first 8 layers frozen, label smoothing (0.1), gradient clipping, mixed precision, and early stopping. Use a single 90/10 stratified split for more epochs.
When fine-tuning a medium-sized transformer for text classification with limited data.

nodes.title: Use ModernBERT-large with proper training regularization
nodes.action: Fine-tune ModernBERT-large with AdamW (lr=2e-5, weight_decay=0.01), cosine annealing with warm restarts, gradient accumulation (2 steps), gradient clipping (max_norm=1.0), mixed precision, and early stopping (patience=3). Use stratified 85/15 split.
applies_when: When using ModernBERT-large for text classification and needing to mitigate overfitting.
nodes.text:
Use ModernBERT-large with proper training regularization
Fine-tune ModernBERT-large with AdamW (lr=2e-5, weight_decay=0.01), cosine annealing with warm restarts, gradient accumulation (2 steps), gradient clipping (max_norm=1.0), mixed precision, and early stopping (patience=3). Use stratified 85/15 split.
When using ModernBERT-large for text classification and needing to mitigate overfitting.

nodes.title: Combine multiple frozen transformer embeddings with XGBoost
nodes.action: Extract [CLS] embeddings from multiple frozen transformers (e.g., DeBERTa-v3-base, RoBERTa-base, DistilBERT-base), concatenate them, and train an XGBoost classifier with stratified 5-fold cross-validation and early stopping.
applies_when: When aiming for high performance without fine-tuning, leveraging diverse representations.
nodes.text:
Combine multiple frozen transformer embeddings with XGBoost
Extract [CLS] embeddings from multiple frozen transformers (e.g., DeBERTa-v3-base, RoBERTa-base, DistilBERT-base), concatenate them, and train an XGBoost classifier with stratified 5-fold cross-validation and early stopping.
When aiming for high performance without fine-tuning, leveraging diverse representations.

nodes.title: Use XGBoost with hist tree method for CPU compatibility
nodes.action: Set XGBoost tree_method='hist' instead of 'gpu_hist' to avoid GPU compatibility issues, and move early_stopping_rounds to the constructor for older XGBoost versions.
applies_when: When using XGBoost and encountering 'gpu_hist not supported' or 'early_stopping_rounds' parameter errors.
nodes.text:

nodes.title: Define variables before use in training scripts
nodes.action: Ensure all variables (e.g., train_loader, num_epochs) are defined before they are referenced, especially when setting up schedulers or computing total steps.
applies_when: When writing training loops that depend on DataLoaders or epoch counts.
nodes.text:
Define variables before use in training scripts

nodes.title: Access transformer backbone attributes correctly
nodes.action: When freezing or accessing transformer backbone parameters, use the correct attribute name (e.g., model.bert for BERT, model.model for ModernBERT). Check the model's source or documentation.
applies_when: When working with HuggingFace transformer models and needing to access internal layers.
nodes.text:
Access transformer backbone attributes correctly
When freezing or accessing transformer backbone parameters, use the correct attribute name (e.g., model.bert for BERT, model.model for ModernBERT). Check the model's source or documentation.

nodes.title: Use CrossEntropyLoss with label_smoothing instead of LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy
nodes.action: Use torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss with the label_smoothing parameter instead of importing LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy from transformers, which may not be available.
applies_when: When label smoothing is needed and the transformers library version may not support LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy.
nodes.text:
Use CrossEntropyLoss with label_smoothing instead of LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy
Use torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss with the label_smoothing parameter instead of importing LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy from transformers, which may not be available.
When label smoothing is needed and the transformers library version may not support LabelSmoothingCrossEntropy.

nodes.title: Use smaller SentenceTransformer model to avoid CUDA OOM
nodes.action: Replace large SentenceTransformer models (e.g., all-mpnet-base-v2, 768-dim) with smaller ones (e.g., all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-dim) to reduce GPU memory usage and avoid CUDA out-of-memory errors during embedding extraction.
applies_when: When extracting Sentence-BERT embeddings on a GPU with limited free memory due to other processes.
nodes.text:
Use smaller SentenceTransformer model to avoid CUDA OOM
Replace large SentenceTransformer models (e.g., all-mpnet-base-v2, 768-dim) with smaller ones (e.g., all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-dim) to reduce GPU memory usage and avoid CUDA out-of-memory errors during embedding extraction.
When extracting Sentence-BERT embeddings on a GPU with limited free memory due to other processes.

nodes.title: Force SentenceTransformer to use CPU to avoid GPU OOM
nodes.action: Initialize SentenceTransformer with device='cpu' to avoid GPU memory contention when other processes occupy most VRAM.
applies_when: When GPU memory is insufficient for loading a SentenceTransformer model due to other processes.
nodes.text:
Force SentenceTransformer to use CPU to avoid GPU OOM
Initialize SentenceTransformer with device='cpu' to avoid GPU memory contention when other processes occupy most VRAM.
When GPU memory is insufficient for loading a SentenceTransformer model due to other processes.

nodes.title: Set DataLoader num_workers=0 to avoid shared memory issues
nodes.action: Set num_workers=0 in DataLoader (and optionally pin_memory=False) to prevent 'No space left on device' or CUDA bus errors caused by limited shared memory (/dev/shm) in containerized environments.
applies_when: When encountering 'Bus error' or 'No space left on device' during DataLoader worker initialization, or when using multiprocessing with limited shared memory.
nodes.text:
Set DataLoader num_workers=0 to avoid shared memory issues
Set num_workers=0 in DataLoader (and optionally pin_memory=False) to prevent 'No space left on device' or CUDA bus errors caused by limited shared memory (/dev/shm) in containerized environments.

nodes.title: Disable gradient checkpointing when using gradient accumulation
nodes.action: Disable gradient_checkpointing_enable() when using gradient accumulation with AMP, as it causes 'Trying to backward through the graph a second time' errors. Instead, reduce batch size to manage memory.
applies_when: When training a transformer model with gradient accumulation and mixed precision, and encountering backward pass errors.
nodes.text:
Disable gradient checkpointing when using gradient accumulation
Disable gradient_checkpointing_enable() when using gradient accumulation with AMP, as it causes 'Trying to backward through the graph a second time' errors. Instead, reduce batch size to manage memory.
When training a transformer model with gradient accumulation and mixed precision, and encountering backward pass errors.

nodes.title: Use AdamW from torch.optim instead of transformers
nodes.action: Import AdamW from torch.optim (from torch.optim import AdamW) rather than from transformers to avoid ImportError due to version incompatibility in newer versions of transformers.
applies_when: When using AdamW optimizer in a training script or with HuggingFace transformers.
nodes.text:
Use AdamW from torch.optim instead of transformers
Import AdamW from torch.optim (from torch.optim import AdamW) rather than from transformers to avoid ImportError due to version incompatibility in newer versions of transformers.
When using AdamW optimizer in a training script or with HuggingFace transformers.

nodes.title: Pass model config via DistilBertConfig object
nodes.action: When modifying dropout probabilities for DistilBERT, create a DistilBertConfig object with desired parameters and pass it to from_pretrained via config=config, not as direct keyword arguments.
applies_when: When customizing dropout or other config parameters for DistilBERT model.
nodes.text:
Pass model config via DistilBertConfig object

nodes.title: Re-register EMA after unfreezing backbone layers
nodes.action: When using Exponential Moving Average (EMA) with two-stage fine-tuning, re-register EMA parameters after unfreezing backbone layers to include newly trainable parameters in the shadow dictionary.
applies_when: When using EMA with staged unfreezing where backbone parameters become trainable after initial registration.
nodes.text:
Re-register EMA after unfreezing backbone layers

nodes.title: Match model input dimension to actual feature dimension
nodes.action: Ensure the model's input dimension exactly matches the concatenated feature vector dimension. Compute the actual dimension after all feature extraction steps and set input_dim accordingly.
applies_when: When building a model that takes concatenated features from multiple sources (e.g., SBERT + TF-IDF + stylometric).
nodes.text:
Match model input dimension to actual feature dimension

nodes.title: Define all variables before use in script
nodes.action: Ensure all variables are defined before they are referenced, especially when using functions that return multiple values. Assign returned vectorizers, embeddings, etc. to named variables in the correct order.
applies_when: When writing a long script with multiple feature extraction steps and function calls.
nodes.text:
Define all variables before use in script

nodes.title: Use two-stage fine-tuning with frozen backbone then full fine-tuning
nodes.action: First train only the classifier head and gating network with frozen backbone for a few epochs, then unfreeze all layers for full fine-tuning. This prevents overfitting and improves generalization.
applies_when: When fine-tuning a transformer on a small dataset to avoid overfitting.
nodes.text:
Use two-stage fine-tuning with frozen backbone then full fine-tuning

nodes.title: Use multi-layer CLS aggregation with learned gating
nodes.action: Aggregate [CLS] tokens from multiple transformer layers (e.g., last 3 or all 6) using a learnable gating mechanism to combine layer representations, improving feature richness.
applies_when: When using a transformer backbone for classification and wanting to leverage intermediate representations.
nodes.text:
Use multi-layer CLS aggregation with learned gating
Aggregate [CLS] tokens from multiple transformer layers (e.g., last 3 or all 6) using a learnable gating mechanism to combine layer representations, improving feature richness.

nodes.title: Use ensemble of DistilBERT, XGBoost on TF-IDF, and CharCNN-LSTM
nodes.action: Combine predictions from a fine-tuned DistilBERT, an XGBoost model trained on TF-IDF + stylistic features, and a character-level CNN-LSTM, weighted by validation performance. This ensemble breaks plateaus.
applies_when: When a single model's validation log-loss plateaus and additional diversity is needed.
nodes.text:
Use ensemble of DistilBERT, XGBoost on TF-IDF, and CharCNN-LSTM

nodes.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-small with gradient checkpointing disabled and reduced batch size
nodes.action: Use DeBERTa-v3-small instead of large/base to fit in GPU memory. Disable gradient checkpointing to avoid backward pass errors, and reduce batch size to manage memory.
applies_when: When fine-tuning a DeBERTa model on a GPU with limited memory and encountering OOM or gradient checkpointing conflicts.
nodes.text:

nodes.title: Use 5-fold cross-validation with MiniLM transformer and sparse features
nodes.action: Train a MiniLM transformer fused with sparse TF-IDF and stylistic features using 5-fold cross-validation, averaging predictions across folds for better generalization.
applies_when: When aiming for robust performance on a small text classification dataset.
nodes.text:
Use 5-fold cross-validation with MiniLM transformer and sparse features

nodes.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-large with ensemble of XGBoost and Logistic Regression for best performance
nodes.action: Fine-tune DeBERTa-v3-large with AdamW, linear warmup, mixed precision, gradient clipping, label smoothing, and early stopping. Combine its embeddings with engineered features (stylometric, readability, POS, n-grams) and train XGBoost and Logistic Regression, then optimize ensemble weights via validation log loss.
applies_when: When aiming for top performance on text classification tasks with sufficient GPU memory and training time.
nodes.text:

nodes.title: Use RoBERTa-base with proper initialization (avoid passing dropout directly to from_pretrained)
nodes.action: When using RobertaForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(), do not pass 'dropout' or 'attention_dropout' as keyword arguments; instead, configure dropout after loading the model by modifying model.config.
applies_when: When initializing a RoBERTa model for sequence classification.

nodes.title: Use DistilBERT with partial freezing and label smoothing for moderate performance
nodes.action: Freeze first 4 of 6 transformer layers, use CrossEntropyLoss with label_smoothing=0.1, AdamW optimizer, cosine scheduler with warmup, gradient accumulation, and mixed precision. Train with early stopping.
applies_when: When using DistilBERT for text classification with limited compute and moderate accuracy requirements.
nodes.text:

nodes.title: Use MLP with engineered features and Sentence-BERT embeddings for baseline
nodes.action: Extract lexical, syntactic, stopword, structural, and char TF-IDF features, combine with Sentence-BERT embeddings (all-mpnet-base-v2), and train a 3-layer MLP with LayerNorm, dropout, and AdamW. Use cosine annealing scheduler and early stopping.
applies_when: When building a strong baseline without fine-tuning a large transformer.
nodes.text:

nodes.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-base with multi-task learning and contrastive loss disabled
nodes.action: Use DeBERTa-v3-base with a classification head, disable contrastive loss to avoid NaN, use AdamW with linear warmup, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, and early stopping. Ensure checkpoint loading uses the exact saved filename.
applies_when: When using DeBERTa-v3-base with multi-task learning; disable contrastive loss if numerical instability occurs.
nodes.text:
Use DeBERTa-v3-base with multi-task learning and contrastive loss disabled

When using DeBERTa-v3-base with multi-task learning; disable contrastive loss if numerical instability occurs.

nodes.title: Use word-level perturbation augmentation (random swap/delete) instead of synonym replacement
nodes.action: Apply mild word-level augmentation: random token swap (probability 0.1) and random token deletion (probability 0.1) to training texts. This regularizes without distorting authorial style.
applies_when: When augmenting text data for authorship attribution; avoid synonym replacement which can alter author voice.
nodes.text:

nodes.title: Use CosineAnnealingWarmRestarts scheduler with linear warmup for transformer fine-tuning
nodes.action: Use a cosine annealing scheduler with linear warmup (e.g., warmup_steps=500) and restarts (T_0=10, T_mult=2) to improve generalization and escape plateaus.
applies_when: When fine-tuning transformer models for text classification.

nodes.title: Use ModernBERT-large with proper dropout configuration via config object
nodes.action: Load ModernBertForSequenceClassification without dropout kwargs, then set dropout via model.config.hidden_dropout_prob and model.config.attention_probs_dropout_prob after loading.
applies_when: When using ModernBERT from HuggingFace and needing to adjust dropout probabilities.
nodes.text:
Use ModernBERT-large with proper dropout configuration via config object

nodes.title: Access ModernBERT backbone via model.model attribute
nodes.action: For ModernBertForSequenceClassification, the underlying encoder is accessed via model.model (not model.bert or model.modern_bert). In a custom subclass, use self.model.encoder.layer for layer-wise operations.
applies_when: When implementing custom forward passes, progressive unfreezing, or creating a custom model that wraps ModernBertForSequenceClassification.
nodes.text:
Access ModernBERT backbone via model.model attribute

nodes.title: Use progressive unfreezing with linear decay and single optimizer to prevent overfitting
nodes.action: Start with only the classifier head trainable, then gradually unfreeze encoder layers (e.g., last 4 layers after epoch 2, next 4 after epoch 3) without recreating the optimizer; use a single AdamW optimizer with differential learning rates (classifier LR = backbone LR * 5-10).
applies_when: When fine-tuning a large transformer (ModernBERT, RoBERTa, etc.) on a small dataset to avoid catastrophic overfitting.
nodes.text:
Use progressive unfreezing with linear decay and single optimizer to prevent overfitting

When fine-tuning a large transformer (ModernBERT, RoBERTa, etc.) on a small dataset to avoid catastrophic overfitting.

nodes.title: Combine multiple frozen transformer embeddings with XGBoost stacking
nodes.action: Extract embeddings from several pretrained transformers (e.g., RoBERTa, DeBERTa, ALBERT) using mean pooling, then train an XGBoost classifier on the concatenated embeddings with probability outputs from base models as additional features.
applies_when: When aiming for best performance on text classification with limited compute; ensemble of diverse transformers improves generalization.
nodes.text:
Combine multiple frozen transformer embeddings with XGBoost stacking
Extract embeddings from several pretrained transformers (e.g., RoBERTa, DeBERTa, ALBERT) using mean pooling, then train an XGBoost classifier on the concatenated embeddings with probability outputs from base models as additional features.
When aiming for best performance on text classification with limited compute; ensemble of diverse transformers improves generalization.

nodes.title: Use weighted ensemble averaging of transformer predictions
nodes.action: Average the softmax probabilities from multiple fine-tuned transformers (e.g., 0.5 DistilBERT + 0.5 RoBERTa) to produce final predictions; tune weights on validation set.
applies_when: When individual transformer models show complementary strengths and overfitting patterns.
nodes.text:
Use weighted ensemble averaging of transformer predictions
Average the softmax probabilities from multiple fine-tuned transformers (e.g., 0.5 DistilBERT + 0.5 RoBERTa) to produce final predictions; tune weights on validation set.
When individual transformer models show complementary strengths and overfitting patterns.

nodes.title: Use stratified K-fold cross-validation to ensure balanced validation splits
nodes.action: Use StratifiedKFold from sklearn to split the training data into folds that preserve the class distribution; use one fold for validation and the rest for training.
applies_when: When dealing with imbalanced classification tasks to ensure representative validation metrics.
nodes.text:
Use stratified K-fold cross-validation to ensure balanced validation splits
Use StratifiedKFold from sklearn to split the training data into folds that preserve the class distribution; use one fold for validation and the rest for training.
When dealing with imbalanced classification tasks to ensure representative validation metrics.

nodes.title: Use label smoothing in CrossEntropyLoss to prevent overconfidence
nodes.action: Set CrossEntropyLoss with label_smoothing=0.1 to penalize overconfident predictions and improve generalization.
applies_when: When training classification models prone to overfitting, especially with large transformers.
nodes.text:
Use label smoothing in CrossEntropyLoss to prevent overconfidence
Set CrossEntropyLoss with label_smoothing=0.1 to penalize overconfident predictions and improve generalization.
When training classification models prone to overfitting, especially with large transformers.

nodes.title: Use mixed precision training with GradScaler for memory efficiency
nodes.action: Enable automatic mixed precision (AMP) with torch.cuda.amp.autocast and GradScaler to reduce GPU memory usage and speed up training without significant accuracy loss.
applies_when: When training large transformer models on GPU with limited memory.
nodes.text:
Use mixed precision training with GradScaler for memory efficiency
Enable automatic mixed precision (AMP) with torch.cuda.amp.autocast and GradScaler to reduce GPU memory usage and speed up training without significant accuracy loss.
When training large transformer models on GPU with limited memory.

nodes.title: Use gradient accumulation to simulate larger batch size
nodes.action: Accumulate gradients over multiple forward/backward passes (e.g., 2 steps) before performing an optimizer step, with effective batch size = per_device_batch_size * accumulation_steps, to increase batch size without extra memory.
applies_when: When GPU memory is insufficient or limited for desired batch size during transformer training.
nodes.text:
Use gradient accumulation to simulate larger batch size
Accumulate gradients over multiple forward/backward passes (e.g., 2 steps) before performing an optimizer step, with effective batch size = per_device_batch_size * accumulation_steps, to increase batch size without extra memory.
When GPU memory is insufficient or limited for desired batch size during transformer training.

nodes.title: Use early stopping with patience based on validation loss
nodes.action: Monitor validation loss and stop training if no improvement for a set number of epochs (e.g., patience=3); save the best model checkpoint.
applies_when: When training deep learning models to prevent overfitting and save time.
nodes.text:
Use early stopping with patience based on validation loss
Monitor validation loss and stop training if no improvement for a set number of epochs (e.g., patience=3); save the best model checkpoint.
When training deep learning models to prevent overfitting and save time.

nodes.title: Use Stochastic Weight Averaging (SWA) to improve generalization
nodes.action: After training, average model weights from the last few epochs (e.g., last 5) using SWA to obtain a smoother solution that generalizes better.
applies_when: When fine-tuning transformers and validation loss plateaus or oscillates.
nodes.text:
Use Stochastic Weight Averaging (SWA) to improve generalization
After training, average model weights from the last few epochs (e.g., last 5) using SWA to obtain a smoother solution that generalizes better.

nodes.title: Use gradient clipping to stabilize training

applies_when: When training deep networks, especially transformers, to avoid training instability or gradient explosion.

nodes.action: When using a custom model (not HuggingFace AutoModel), ensure the forward method returns logits in a format consistent with the training loop. This provides a robust baseline that avoids overfitting on small datasets.
applies_when: When starting a text classification task with limited data and need a quick, non-overfitting baseline.

nodes.title: Escape regex special characters in str.count for parenthesis counting
nodes.action: When counting parentheses in text using str.count, use literal strings (e.g., '(' and ')') as str.count does not interpret regex. However, if using regex functions like re.findall, escape parentheses with backslash. In pandas, str.count with '(' works correctly as it treats the argument as a literal string, not a regex pattern.
applies_when: When counting special characters like parentheses in text data using pandas str.count.

In attention pooling or similar modules, when using masked_fill with a large negative value (e.g., -1e9) under mixed precision (float16), replace with a smaller negative value like -1e4 that can be represented in float16 without overflow.
When using mixed precision training (autocast) and masked_fill with a large negative value causes overflow in float16.

nodes.title: Use progressive unfreezing with warm-up and differential learning rates to improve generalization
nodes.action: Train transformer models in phases: first freeze backbone and train only the head for a few epochs, then gradually unfreeze layers with lower learning rates (e.g., 1e-6 for backbone, 2e-5 for head) and use a warm-up phase to stabilize training.
applies_when: When fine-tuning a large transformer model to prevent overfitting and improve validation loss.

nodes.title: Use two-phase training with different stratified splits to improve performance
nodes.action: Train in two phases: Phase 1 on a stratified split (e.g., 17k train / 500 val) with warm-up and differential learning rates, then Phase 2 on a different stratified split to leverage more data and reduce overfitting.
applies_when: When aiming for best performance on a small dataset with a transformer model.

nodes.title: Combine engineered features with transformer embeddings for hybrid model
nodes.action: Extract handcrafted features (text statistics, n-grams, POS, sentiment, author-specific vocabulary) and concatenate them with transformer [CLS] embeddings or use them as input to a secondary model (e.g., LightGBM) for ensemble.
applies_when: When building a strong classifier for text classification tasks with limited data.

nodes.title: Use multi-scale convolutional block and attention pooling on transformer hidden states
nodes.action: Apply multiple parallel 1D convolutions with different kernel sizes (e.g., 2,3,5,7) followed by adaptive max pooling and attention pooling on transformer hidden states to capture multi-scale features before classification.
applies_when: When designing a custom head for a transformer model to improve sequence representation.

nodes.action: Train separate models on each fold of a 5-fold stratified split and average their predictions (or use a meta-model) to reduce variance and improve test performance.

nodes.title: Use synonym replacement augmentation via WordNet to reduce overfitting

nodes.title: Reduce model size or batch size to avoid CUDA OOM
nodes.action: Use a smaller model variant (e.g., DeBERTa-v3-small instead of base) or reduce batch size to fit GPU memory. Disable gradient checkpointing if it conflicts with gradient accumulation.

nodes.title: Avoid rebuilding optimizer mid-training to prevent memory leaks
nodes.action: Do not recreate the optimizer or scheduler during training (e.g., at progressive unfreezing stages). Instead, update parameter groups in-place or use a single optimizer throughout.
applies_when: When implementing progressive unfreezing or multi-stage training that would normally require rebuilding the optimizer.

nodes.action: Train the entire model from the start with a lower learning rate for the backbone, avoiding progressive unfreezing which can cause memory spikes when unfreezing layers.
applies_when: When progressive unfreezing leads to CUDA OOM at later stages due to increased memory usage from unfrozen layers.

nodes.action: Use fewer gradient accumulation steps (e.g., 2 instead of 4) to reduce peak GPU memory usage during training.

nodes.action: Use a simpler classification head (e.g., mean pooling + linear layer) instead of multi-scale Conv1D blocks to reduce model memory usage.
applies_when: When the model architecture includes memory-intensive components like multi-scale convolutions and CUDA OOM occurs.

nodes.title: Use DistilBERT with label smoothing and warmup cosine annealing for text classification
nodes.action: Use DistilBERT-base-uncased with a classification head, AdamW optimizer (2e-5 for BERT, 1e-3 for head), linear warmup for 10% of epochs, cosine annealing scheduler, mixed precision (AMP), gradient clipping (norm=1.0), label smoothing (0.1), and early stopping (patience=3) to achieve strong validation log loss.
applies_when: When performing text classification on a small-to-medium dataset (e.g., author identification) and seeking a strong transformer baseline.

nodes.title: Use MLP with TF-IDF and stylometric features for text classification baseline
nodes.action: Extract stylometric features (word/sentence length statistics, punctuation ratios, POS counts), character n-gram TF-IDF (2-5), word n-gram TF-IDF (1-3), scale with StandardScaler, and train a 3-layer MLP (512-256-128) with BatchNorm, GELU, dropout, AdamW, cosine annealing warm restarts, mixed precision, label smoothing, and early stopping.
applies_when: When building a strong non-transformer baseline for text classification tasks with limited data.

nodes.title: Use TextCNN with random embeddings and stylometric features for text classification
nodes.action: Tokenize text, build vocabulary, use trainable random embeddings (128-dim) with Xavier initialization, apply multi-filter CNN (kernel sizes 2,3,4,5, 128 filters each) with batch norm, ReLU, global max pooling, dropout (0.3), combine with 6 stylometric features via MLP branch, train with label smoothing cross-entropy, AdamW, and early stopping.
applies_when: When transformer models are unavailable or too slow, and a CNN-based approach is preferred for text classification.

nodes.title: Use handcrafted stylometric features for authorship attribution
nodes.action: Extract 26 stylometric features including word-level statistics (avg word length, sentence length), punctuation density, stopword ratio, type-token ratio, readability indices (Coleman-Lieu, Flesch), lexical richness measures, and normalize with StandardScaler.
applies_when: When performing authorship attribution or style-based text classification to capture writing style signals.

nodes.title: Avoid NaN predictions by simplifying attention mechanisms and using gradient clipping
nodes.action: When using complex attention pooling (e.g., weighted layer attention, multi-head attention) with mixed precision, simplify architecture or add gradient clipping (norm=1.0) and torch.nan_to_num to prevent NaN outputs.

nodes.action: When accessing encoder layers of DeBERTa-v3-large via AutoModel, use model.backbone.encoder.layer (not model.backbone.deberta.encoder.layer) because AutoModel returns the backbone directly.

nodes.title: Use correct indexing for StratifiedKFold splits
nodes.action: When using StratifiedKFold, ensure that the indices from split() are applied to the full dataset, not to a subset that has already been reduced in size, to avoid IndexError.
applies_when: When performing cross-validation with StratifiedKFold on a dataset that has been pre-filtered or partially indexed.

nodes.action: Instead of relying on external GloVe embedding files (e.g., glove.6B.300d.txt) or torch.hub/torchtext GloVe loaders, use trainable random embeddings with Xavier initialization to avoid FileNotFoundError or download failures.

nodes.action: When fine-tuning a transformer model, first train with frozen backbone for a few epochs, then unfreeze all parameters and continue training with a lower learning rate. Ensure all tensors are on the same device and use gradient clipping to avoid CUDA errors.

nodes.action: When creating test dataset tensors, verify that the number of test samples matches across all feature arrays (e.g., test_features, test_input_ids). Avoid computing test features on combined train+test data.

nodes.action: When creating a PyTorch Dataset for classification, ensure labels are integer-encoded (e.g., via LabelEncoder) before passing to the dataset, not raw string labels.

nodes.action: When saving model checkpoints, move tensors to CPU first (model.to('cpu')) to avoid file write errors that can occur with GPU tensors in multi-worker settings.

nodes.action: Train in two phases: Phase 1 freezes all transformer layers and trains only the classification head for a few epochs; Phase 2 unfreezes selected layers (e.g., last 4-8) and fine-tunes with a lower learning rate. Use separate optimizers or parameter groups with differential learning rates.
applies_when: When fine-tuning a large pretrained transformer on a small dataset to prevent overfitting and stabilize training.

nodes.action: Concatenate the [CLS] token embedding with projected engineered features (e.g., stylometric, TF-IDF) and pass through a simple MLP classifier. Avoid multi-head cross-attention or gated fusion mechanisms that introduce instability and overfitting.

nodes.action: Ensure the model's forward method returns logits as a tensor directly, or as an object with a .logits attribute, consistently across all code paths. Avoid returning tuples or dictionaries that may break downstream loss computation.

nodes.action: Call scaler.unscale_(optimizer) only once per gradient accumulation step, and not before FGM attack if scaler.step will call it automatically, to prevent RuntimeError.

Optimize ensemble weights via grid search on validation log loss.

nodes.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-large with mean pooling, multi-sample dropout, and Focal Loss for robust text classification
nodes.action: Use DeBERTa-v3-large backbone with mean pooling of hidden states, multi-sample dropout (4 samples), and a simple linear classifier head. Train with Focal Loss (gamma=2.0), AdamW optimizer, mixed precision (AMP), gradient clipping, linear warmup, and ReduceLROnPlateau scheduler. Use 5-fold stratified cross-validation and early stopping.
applies_when: When performing text classification with a transformer model and needing strong regularization to prevent overfitting, or when fine-tuning DeBERTa-v3-large for a stable baseline.

nodes.action: Split training data into 5 stratified folds. For each fold, train a model on 4 folds and validate on the held-out fold, using early stopping to prevent overfitting. Average predictions from all folds for the test set.
applies_when: When building a robust model for small-to-medium datasets, needing to reduce variance, and having sufficient compute time.

nodes.action: Apply mean pooling over all token hidden states from the last transformer layer (or last two layers) to obtain a fixed-size sentence embedding. Use this embedding as input to a classifier head.
applies_when: When using a transformer model for text classification and CLS token representation is suboptimal.

nodes.title: Use early stopping with patience based on validation loss to prevent overfitting
nodes.action: Monitor validation loss after each epoch. Stop training if validation loss does not improve for a set number of epochs (patience). Restore model weights from the best epoch.
applies_when: When training neural networks and needing to prevent overfitting by stopping at the optimal point.

nodes.action: Use AdamW from torch.optim with weight decay (e.g., 0.01) and separate parameter groups for bias and LayerNorm terms (no decay).

nodes.action: Ensure that parameter groups for differential learning rates are mutually exclusive. Use set operations to verify no parameter appears in multiple groups before creating the optimizer.

nodes.action: Do not wrap operations that require gradients with torch.no_grad() inside an autocast context. If MixUp or similar augmentation requires no_grad, compute it outside the training loop or on logits after forward pass.
applies_when: When implementing data augmentation that mixes samples (e.g., MixUp) and using mixed precision training.

nodes.action: After creating custom layers (e.g., nn.Linear), explicitly move them to the target device using .to(device) or ensure they are created after the model is moved.

nodes.action: For DistilRoBERTa, access layers via model.roberta.encoder.layer. For DeBERTa-v3, access via model.deberta.encoder.layer. Verify the correct attribute path for the specific model variant.

nodes.action: When building multi-encoder models, compute the total feature dimension by running a dummy forward pass or carefully summing encoder output dimensions. Verify that the classifier's first linear layer input size matches the actual concatenated feature size.

nodes.action: Train DeBERTa-v3-large with label smoothing (0.1), linear warmup scheduler, gradient accumulation (4 steps), and mixed precision. nodes.action: After training a transformer (e.g., RoBERTa, DeBERTa), extract pooled embeddings from the best checkpoint. Use the LightGBM predictions as a meta-learner to improve ensemble performance.

nodes.title: Use DeBERTa-v3-base with mean pooling and simple MLP classifier for stable fine-tuning
nodes.action: Load DeBERTa-v3-base with AutoModel (not AutoModelForSequenceClassification). Apply mean pooling over token embeddings (excluding padding). Add a 2-layer MLP classifier (e.g., hidden size 256) with dropout. Train with cross-entropy loss (label smoothing 0.1), AdamW (lr 2e-5), cosine scheduler with warmup, gradient accumulation (4 steps), and mixed precision. Use early stopping on validation log-loss.
applies_when: When a moderate-sized transformer is needed to avoid CUDA OOM while still achieving good performance on text classification.

nodes.title: Use focal loss with label smoothing to handle class imbalance and improve calibration
nodes.action: Replace standard cross-entropy with focal loss (gamma=2, alpha=None) combined with label smoothing (epsilon=0.1). This reduces the loss contribution from well-classified examples and prevents overconfidence.
applies_when: When dealing with imbalanced classes or when the model produces overconfident predictions (e.g., validation log-loss plateaus).

nodes.title: Avoid complex multi-task losses (contrastive, center loss) that cause dimension mismatches
nodes.action: Stick to simple cross-entropy or focal loss with label smoothing. If using additional losses, ensure embedding dimensions match exactly (e.g., projection head output dim equals centers dim).
applies_when: When designing loss functions for transformer-based classifiers; complex losses often introduce bugs and may not improve performance.

When designing loss functions for transformer-based classifiers; complex losses often introduce bugs and may not improve performance.

nodes.title: Ensure model forward method returns logits consistently for evaluation
nodes.action: Define model forward to return a tuple (logits, pooled) or a single tensor. Ensure evaluate() function unpacks the correct number of outputs. Avoid multiple evaluate() definitions that expect different return signatures.
applies_when: When implementing custom model forward and evaluation loops; mismatched return signatures cause runtime errors.

nodes.title: Avoid leaving stray text comments outside of comment blocks in Python code

nodes.title: Use torch.save(model.state_dict(), ...) and load with model.load_state_dict(...) to avoid pooler mismatch
nodes.action: Save only the state_dict (not the full model) and load it into the model instance. Ensure the model architecture (including pooler) is consistent between save and load. For DeBERTa, avoid expecting a pooler layer if using AutoModelForSequenceClassification.
applies_when: When checkpointing and reloading transformer models; saving full model can cause key mismatches if architecture changes.
nodes.text:

nodes.title: Avoid data augmentation that creates size mismatch between features and labels
nodes.action: When applying back-translation or other augmentation, ensure that the number of augmented samples matches the number of labels. Duplicate labels accordingly or use a dataset that handles augmentation internally.
applies_when: When augmenting text data; mismatched sizes cause TensorDataset creation errors.

nodes.title: Use smaller model variant (DeBERTa-v3-base) to avoid CUDA OOM when compute is limited
nodes.action: If DeBERTa-v3-large causes out-of-memory errors or timeouts, switch to DeBERTa-v3-base with similar training setup (mean pooling, label smoothing, gradient accumulation).
applies_when: When GPU memory is insufficient for large transformer models; base model still achieves competitive performance.
nodes.text:

nodes.title: Avoid progressive unfreezing that causes NaN losses due to optimizer re-initialization
nodes.action: If using progressive unfreezing, do not recreate the optimizer mid-training. Instead, adjust learning rates for different parameter groups before training starts, or use a single learning rate for all layers.
applies_when: When fine-tuning transformers with layer-wise training; recreating optimizer can lead to instability and NaN losses.
nodes.text:

nodes.title: Verify each sub-goal succeeds before proceeding in multi-stage pipelines
nodes.action: After each stage (feature extraction, model training, checkpoint saving, embedding extraction), print confirmation or check outputs. Ensure no silent failures before moving to next stage.
applies_when: When building complex multi-stage pipelines; early detection of bugs prevents wasted compute.

nodes.title: Initialize optimizer before training loop to avoid NameError

nodes.title: Use correct attribute name for ModernBERT embedding layer
nodes.action: Access ModernBERT's embedding layer via model.model.embeddings.tok_embeddings, not word_embeddings.
applies_when: When implementing mixup or other techniques that require direct access to the embedding layer of ModernBERT.

nodes.title: Avoid FGM adversarial training with torch.compile or retain_graph=True
nodes.action: Remove FGM adversarial training or ensure backward passes do not use retain_graph=True when using torch.compile.
applies_when: When using ModernBERT with torch.compile and adversarial training.
nodes.text:

nodes.title: Move loss function weights to same device as input tensors
nodes.action: Ensure all buffers in custom loss functions (e.g., AdaptiveFocalLoss.weights) are moved to the same device as the input tensors.
applies_when: When implementing custom loss functions that use per-class weights.

nodes.title: Use progressive unfreezing with EMA and FGM for stable fine-tuning
nodes.action: Freeze backbone initially, then progressively unfreeze layers while using EMA and FGM adversarial training to stabilize training and improve generalization.

nodes.action: Use focal loss with adaptive gamma and label smoothing to handle class imbalance and improve calibration.
applies_when: When dealing with imbalanced text classification tasks.

applies_when: When training large transformers with limited GPU memory.

nodes.title: Use TF-IDF features with n-grams up to 3 for text classification baseline
nodes.action: Extract TF-IDF features with unigram, bigram, and trigram ranges (max 5000 features) as a strong baseline.

nodes.title: Use temporal ensemble of top-K checkpoints for transformer predictions
nodes.action: After fine-tuning, average the predicted probabilities from the top-K checkpoints (e.g., top 3 by validation log loss) using inverse log-loss weighting to stabilize predictions and improve calibration.
applies_when: When fine-tuning a transformer model and the best single checkpoint shows high variance or overfitting.

nodes.title: Save model checkpoints based on validation log loss instead of cross-entropy loss
nodes.action: Monitor and save the model checkpoint that achieves the lowest validation log loss (the competition metric), not the lowest cross-entropy loss, to directly optimize the target metric.
applies_when: When the evaluation metric is log loss and the model's cross-entropy loss does not correlate well with log loss.

nodes.title: Apply temperature scaling to calibrate transformer probabilities before ensembling
nodes.action: After fine-tuning, optimize a temperature parameter on the validation set to scale logits before softmax, improving probability calibration and ensemble performance.
applies_when: When transformer probabilities are overconfident or poorly calibrated, degrading ensemble results.

nodes.title: Use handcrafted stylometric, readability, and POS-approximation features for author identification
nodes.action: Extract 30+ stylometric features (punctuation ratios, word length stats, function word counts, archaic/emotional word ratios), 4 readability features (Flesch score, ARI, syllables, complex word ratio), and 5 POS-approximation features (noun/verb/adj/adv ratios via suffix matching) as additional inputs to XGBoost or ensemble.
applies_when: When working on authorship attribution tasks with limited training data.
nodes.text:

nodes.title: Optimize ensemble weights via grid search on validation log loss
nodes.action: After training individual models, perform a grid search over weight combinations (e.g., step 0.05) to minimize validation log loss, then apply the optimal weights to test predictions.
applies_when: When combining multiple models (transformer, XGBoost, logistic regression) into an ensemble.

nodes.title: Use semi-supervised test set augmentation for n-gram features
nodes.action: Append a fraction (e.g., 10%) of test samples with pseudo-labels to the training set before extracting n-gram TF-IDF features, improving domain adaptation for XGBoost.
applies_when: When n-gram features show distribution shift between train and test sets.

nodes.title: Use multi-layer pooling (weighted average of last hidden layers) for transformer embeddings
nodes.action: Instead of using only the CLS token, compute a weighted average of the last 3-4 hidden layers' token embeddings, then apply mean pooling over tokens to obtain a richer sentence representation.
applies_when: When the CLS token alone does not capture sufficient contextual information for downstream tasks.

nodes.title: Use two-phase training: freeze backbone then full fine-tuning with discriminative learning rates
nodes.action: First train only the classifier head with the backbone frozen for a few epochs, then unfreeze the entire model and fine-tune with layer-wise learning rate decay (e.g., 1.0x for top layers, 0.95x per layer downward) to prevent overfitting.
applies_when: When fine-tuning a large transformer on a small dataset to avoid catastrophic forgetting.

nodes.action: Ensure that every variable, DataLoader, and function is defined earlier in the script than its first usage, especially in multi-stage pipelines where later stages depend on earlier ones.

nodes.title: Ensure model checkpoint architecture matches when saving and loading
nodes.action: When saving a model checkpoint, save only the state_dict and ensure the model architecture used for loading is exactly the same as during saving, including any custom heads or feature fusion layers.
applies_when: When using custom model architectures or when loading a checkpoint into a different model instance.
nodes.text:

nodes.title: Avoid passing unexpected keyword arguments to model forward methods
nodes.action: When calling a custom model's forward method, ensure the method signature accepts all passed arguments; otherwise, modify the forward method to accept **kwargs or pass only expected arguments.
applies_when: When using custom model classes that override the forward method with a restricted signature.
nodes.text:

nodes.title: Use 5-fold stratified cross-validation with OOF predictions for robust ensemble
nodes.action: Implement 5-fold stratified cross-validation to generate out-of-fold (OOF) predictions from each model, then train a meta-learner (e.g., logistic regression) on OOF probabilities to learn ensemble weights. This reduces overfitting and improves generalization compared to a single train/validation split.
applies_when: When building an ensemble of multiple models (e.g., transformer, XGBoost, logistic regression) for classification, and the dataset is small enough to allow multiple training runs.
nodes.text:

nodes.title: Combine handcrafted stylometric features with transformer embeddings for hybrid model
nodes.action: Extract handcrafted features (e.g., text length, punctuation ratios, readability scores, POS approximations) and concatenate them with transformer embeddings (e.g., mean-pooled DeBERTa embeddings). Train an XGBoost classifier on the combined feature set to capture both linguistic and stylistic patterns.
applies_when: When working on authorship attribution or style-based text classification tasks where handcrafted features complement transformer representations.

nodes.title: Use logistic regression as a quick validation baseline and ensemble component
nodes.action: Train a multinomial logistic regression on sparse n-gram features (e.g., TF-IDF) as a fast baseline. Include its predictions in the final ensemble, often with a small weight.
applies_when: When building an ensemble for text classification; logistic regression provides a simple, interpretable model that captures linear patterns.

nodes.action: When initializing LogisticRegression with no penalty, set penalty=None (Python None), not the string 'none'. The string 'none' is invalid and causes an InvalidParameterError.
applies_when: When using scikit-learn's LogisticRegression with penalty=None.
